ledger.why: the game rule for the Naturalist, carried by the game word {@naturalist}

intro.name: The platform
intro.text: (builder), a builder famous for ignoring conventional advice, unveils a structure that seems to defy everything the village knows about weight and balance. A heavy stone platform appears to hang over an empty space with nothing beneath its far edge.

question.name: The challenge
question.text: "That cannot stand," declares the Master Stonewright. "It already is," replies (builder).

choices.label: Test it with a gradually increasing load.
Open it to the public immediately.
Ask the inventor to explain the design.

a1.text:
THE COUNTERWEIGHT:
The builders uncover an ingenious system of buried stones and interlocking beams.

a1_more.text: The platform is safe within carefully measured limits. The critic congratulates (builder) for seeming to defy the world while actually understanding it better than anyone expected.

a2.text:
THE ROOTS:
A living tree's roots anchor the structure.

a2_more.text: It is beautiful and clever, but {@naturalist} warns that the tree's growth could change the balance. The design is modified to protect both the structure and the tree.

a3.text:
THE MIRAGE:
The supposed unsupported edge is an illusion created by a hidden slope and clever stonework.

a3_more.text: The villagers laugh and praise the craftsmanship. The judge declares the illusion a work of art.

b1.text:
THE MIRACLE:
The platform holds an astonishing load without bending.

b1_more.text: (builder) receives the highest praise of the builders, and the village adopts the new technique after independent testing.

b2.text:
THE EMBARRASSMENT:
A single basket of coconuts makes the platform tip into the sand.

b2_more.text: Nobody is hurt. The Master Stonewright folds (stonewright.his/her) arms. "You have indeed defied the laws of building. Unfortunately, the building has objected."

b3.text:
THE UNSETTLING SUCCESS:
The structure remains upright even after its apparent supports are removed.

b3_more.text: The builders cannot explain why. They fence it off for study rather than pretending that mystery proves it is safe.

b4.text:
THE EXPERT WAS WRONG:
The judge's calculations predict failure, but repeated safe tests show the design works.

b4_more.text: The judge checks the assumptions, discovers a mistake, and apologizes. (builder) becomes an advisor to builders.

c1.text:
THE PARADE:
The crowd rushes onto the platform.

c1_more.text: A steward stops them before it is overloaded. The event is postponed until proper testing. (builder) is furious but later admits the steward acted wisely.

c2.text:
THE STUNT:
(builder) walks across the platform while the crowd gasps.

c2_more.text: It holds. The judge says, "A successful gamble is not the same as a sound proof." A formal inspection follows.

c3.text:
THE COLLAPSE:
The platform tilts and settles into soft earth before anyone steps on it.

text_only.reason: the builder's own platform settles; no village structure is damaged

c3_more.text: (builder) becomes a laughingstock and returns to the drawing board, insisting that the next version will be even stranger.

text_only.reason: the builder's own platform settles; no village structure is damaged

d1.text:
THE EXPLANATION:
(builder) presents an intricate account of load, balance and buried counterweights.

d1_more.text: The crowd learns something valuable. A child asks whether the builder can make a roof that stays dry in the rain. "That," says (builder), "would be considerably harder."

d2.text:
THE NON-EXPLANATION:
(builder) says the building stands because it "wants to."

d2_more.text: The Master Stonewright stares. "I require a better explanation." (builder) replies, "So do I." The building is closed pending study.

d3.text:
THE IMPOSSIBLE CLAIM:
(builder) insists that (builder.he/she) has overturned the very order of the world.

d3_more.text: The judges discover a concealed stone brace. (builder) admits it was a dramatic exaggeration. The design remains impressive.
